text: Pierre was right when he said that one must believe in the possibility of happiness in order to be happy, and I now believe in it. Let the dead bury the dead, but while I'm alive, I must live and be happy.
author: Leo Tolstoy

archive.text: However good a Constitution may be, it is sure to turn out bad because those who are called to work it, happen to be a bad lot.
archive.author: B.R. Ambedkar

archive.text: Making with their rhythms something torn and new.
archive.author: Kamau Brathwaite

archive.text: If there were no bad people, there would be no good lawyers.
archive.author: Charles Dickens

archive.text: Nothing can be done at once hastily and prudently.
archive.author: Publilius Syrus

archive.text: Science is the most real guide for civilisation, for life, for success in the world. To search for a guide other than science is absurdity, ignorance and heresy.
archive.author: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk

archive.text: The pedigree of honey does not concern the bee; a clover, any time, to him is aristocracy.
archive.author: Emily Dickinson

archive.text: It's an infernal nuisance to love Life as I do. I seem to love it more as time goes on rather than less. It never becomes a habit to me. It's always a marvel.
archive.author: Katherine Mansfield
